CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left-sided lower back pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient presents with left-sided lower back pain. He reports undergoing back surgery in November 2020 for a microdiscectomy due to a herniated disc that wrapped around and connected to his spinal thecal sac. He initially experienced severe nerve pain radiating down his leg. Currently, he experiences left-sided low back pain that is generally located around the surgical site, though it depends on the day and can occur on the right side as well. Pain is triggered by bending over and occurs randomly. Stretching helps alleviate the pain. Patient reports taking ibuprofen 800 mg daily for pain management. He denies trying ice therapy. On examination, patient has pain with weightbearing and pain with palpation to the left side around L5. No pain with forward flexion, extension, or on the right side with palpation. Dorsiflexion is normal with normal range of motion. No nerve pain or pain down the legs noted. X-ray shows no fractures or issues with spinal bone; surgical site has healed properly.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies pain down legs or current nerve pain.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Back surgery (microdiscectomy) in November 2020 for herniated disc.

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen 800 mg daily.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Patient able to push back against examiner's hands with normal dorsiflexion and normal range of motion. Pain with weightbearing while standing. No pain with forward flexion or extension. Pain with palpation to left side around L5. No pain with palpation to right side.

RESULTS
X-ray of spine: No fractures or bony abnormalities. Surgical site healed properly.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Muscle pull with spinal misalignment. Prescribed physical therapy at VA. Prescribed meloxicam instead of ibuprofen for improved pain management. Referral to pain management for discussion of pain management strategies and non-narcotic options. Prescribed demerol.
